title: August and the Orchard
premise: In the winter of 1889, Ines Sandoval keeps the Point Alder lighthouse alone after her husband's drowning, hiding her late brother-in-law's family — undocumented immigrants fleeing a warrant — in the keeper's cottage. When census taker August Reyes arrives to verify the light station's records, he notices one bed too many and one name too few, and his questions threaten everything. Torn between duty to the government that pays him and the loyalty he owes a woman who once saved his own mother, August must decide whether to report the household before the river ice breaks and the last ferry berth north closes. He falsifies the census at the cost of his career, and Ines gives the final berth not to her blood kin but to her sister-in-law's child, staying behind to keep the light burning through the great storm.
about_author: Paloma Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal light station records along the northern rivers. She writes historical fiction about the quiet people history forgot to count.

chapters.title: The Counting Season
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Establishes the lighthouse routine, the storm season approaching, and the hidden family in the cellar room. Emotional beat: weary vigilance disguised as ordinary competence.

chapters.title: A Man with a Ledger
chapters.summary: August's POV. He arrives by mail boat to conduct the census, all business and cold hands. First meeting with Ines; she lies smoothly about household size. Beat: two careful people measuring each other.

chapters.title: One Bed Too Many
chapters.summary: August's POV. Reviewing old station records, he finds the previous year's log listing four residents; now only one is declared. He says nothing, but begins asking around the village. Beat: suspicion kindled.

chapters.title: Salt and Secrets
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Her nephew Tomás nearly wanders into view during a supply delivery; she covers, but the fear sharpens. Flashback to her husband's drowning and her promise to his brother. Beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: August's POV. Over tea, he asks casually whether anyone else winters at the station. Ines's denial is flawless, but August recognizes the tell of a liar because he was raised by one. Beat: the trap half-sprung.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She visits the village priest who once helped smuggle her brother-in-law across, learning the warrants have grown teeth and a bounty exists for informants. Beat: the stakes become money as well as law.

chapters.title: Ice on the Windows
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV, first departure from the adults. The boy watches the frozen river and asks when they'll cross to the free side. Ines overhears. Beat: innocence forcing the adults' hand.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She negotiates with the ferryman: three berths available before the ice breaks, no more, payment due in full. She has coin for two. Beat: arithmetic becomes cruelty.

chapters.title: August's Mother
chapters.summary: August's POV. A letter from home reveals Ines once sheltered his immigrant mother during a cholera winter — a debt he never knew. His official duty now wars with an unpayable one. Beat: the ground shifts beneath him.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: August's POV. His supervisor announces a surprise audit of the light station's roster. August has days to either report the hidden family or forge federal documents. Beat: point of no return approaching.

chapters.title: The Cellar Room
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She prepares the family to flee, but her sister-in-law Marisol refuses to leave without knowing who betrayed them — and suspects the census taker. Beat: trust fraying inside the sanctuary.

chapters.title: Confession at the Light
chapters.summary: August's POV. He climbs to the lantern room at night and tells Ines what he knows and what he owes. Neither trusts the other, but they strike a wary bargain: he will delay the audit if she decides who sails. Beat: alliance born of mutual leverage.

chapters.title: Three Berths, Four Souls
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The family debates among themselves who should go; Marisol insists Tomás takes a berth, August argues the whole family could scatter overland instead. Beat: love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Villager Rosa's POV. A neighbor, hungry for bounty money, sends word to the marshal about 'extra shadows' at the lighthouse. Beat: betrayal from an unexpected quarter, tightening the noose.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The first great storm hits early; the light fails mid-storm and Ines climbs the tower in hurricane wind to relight it, while the family shelters below. Beat: her competence and sacrifice made visible.

chapters.title: What August Saw
chapters.summary: August's POV. Stranded at the station by the storm, he witnesses Ines's heroism and Marisol's quiet dignity, and burns his original census notes. Beat: conversion — duty redefined as protection.

chapters.title: The Marshal's Sled
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Through the storm window the boy sees sled lights approaching — the marshal, early. August goes out to meet them alone. Beat: terror through a child's eyes.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Climax begins: with the marshal delayed by August's forged paperwork but the ice cracking early, only one berth remains beyond the two paid ones. Ines names the passenger: Tomás. Beat: the choice the blurb promised, made at last.

chapters.title: Breaking
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The river ice booms and splits; Marisol puts her son on the ferry and stays with her husband, choosing her marriage over escape. Ines holds the light for the crossing. Beat: grief and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: August's POV. The inspector arrives to find a clean ledger, a falsified census, and a keeper with a straight spine. August confesses to the forgery alone, shielding Ines, and loses his post. Beat: the price of truth-telling paid in full.

chapters.title: After the Storms
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Spring comes; the light stands, the warrant cools with the marshal's retirement, and a letter arrives from Tomás safe in the north. Marisol and her husband remain, working the station openly under new names. Beat: survival's cost counted, belonging found.

chapters.title: Counted
chapters.summary: August's POV, closing frame. Years later, a new census taker visits Point Alder and records five residents at the light station, all named, none hidden. August, now the ferryman, carries the book himself. Beat: resolution — every soul finally counted.
